question: Why did the workstation check of the fp16-weight ONNX graphs (cosine >= 0.9999, all outputs finite) not reveal DINOv3's fp16 overflow, which made the TensorRT fp16 build produce NaN?
test: dinov3_vitl16.c0.fp16.onnx (fp16 weights, fp32 LayerNorm math) run on onnxruntime 1.31 CPUExecutionProvider with one workstation-preprocessed reference image (outputs/trt_export/pre_desktop.npz)
conclusion: The chunk's hidden state reaches 1.57e5 (> fp16 max 65504) yet stays finite: onnxruntime's CPU provider has no fp16 kernels for these operators and inserts casts, so the residual arithmetic ran in fp32 with fp16-rounded weights. The workstation check therefore validated the weight rounding, not fp16 arithmetic; the overflow could only appear on a backend that computes in fp16 (TensorRT with the FP16 flag).
